fields.Name: WordPress
fields.Description: WordPress self-hosted content and commerce platform connector — syncs core wp/v2 objects (posts, pages, media, taxonomies, users, comments) plus WooCommerce wc/v3 objects (orders, products, customers, coupons) from a per-tenant site URL.

Configuration.AuthFlowNote: HTTP Basic per RFC 7617 with a WordPress APPLICATION PASSWORD: username = the WP user's login, password = the generated application password. Core since WP 5.6, per-user, individually revocable, and it authenticates ANY REST route including wc/v3 (core registers the validator at determine_current_user priority 20 with NO namespace test: wp-includes/default-filters.php:522). AVAILABILITY IS GATED ON TLS from source: wp-includes/user.php:5156 `return is_ssl() || 'local' === wp_get_environment_type();` — unavailable over plain HTTP outside a local environment. There is NO OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow anywhere in the in-scope surface (0 occurrences of 'oauth' in the derived in-scope spec); credentials are entered manually, never refreshed, and do not expire.
Configuration.AuthCredentialTypeNote: DECIDED BY THE IDENTITY STAGE — not re-litigated here. ONE credential type, `WordPress API`, created in metadata (record 21) with schema metadata/credential-types/schemas/wordpress-api.schema.json. `siteUrl` is unconditionally required (self-hosted: there is no vendor host) and the two credential PAIRS are expressed as an `anyOf` — [username, applicationPassword] or [wooConsumerKey, wooConsumerSecret] — because a no-TLS tenant genuinely cannot use an Application Password at all. 🚩 The credential type exists in METADATA ONLY and NOT in the database, so its @lookup will not resolve unless it is pushed with or before this Integration row. DeployPreflight check (4) is where that gets caught.

wooConsumerKeySecret.nonTlsFallback: OAuth 1.0a ONE-LEGGED (HMAC signature over the request: oauth_consumer_key / oauth_timestamp / oauth_nonce / oauth_signature) — the ONLY documented way to reach wc/v3 over plain HTTP.
wooConsumerKeySecret.queryParamFallback: ?consumer_key=&consumer_secret= is accepted AND TAKES PRECEDENCE over the Authorization header, for hosts that strip Authorization. Core Application Passwords have NO query-param fallback — this is the one hard functional advantage of the Woo key pair.
wooConsumerKeySecret.ownPermissionScope: read | write | read_write, enforced per HTTP method in includes/class-wc-rest-authentication.php::check_permissions() (401 woocommerce_rest_authentication_error on mismatch). This scope is INDEPENDENT of WP capabilities.
wooConsumerKeySecret.asymmetryWarning: A Woo consumer key/secret CANNOT read wp/v2 at all — WC_REST_Authentication::is_request_to_rest_api() (Woo 11.0.1:69-83) matches only URIs containing the REST prefix followed by `wc/` or `wc-`. A Woo-only credential yields a WooCommerce-only object set and MUST raise an explicit capability warning, never an empty-but-green sync.

AuthAlternatives.cookieNonce: Cookie authentication + nonce (X-WP-Nonce header or _wpnonce param, action `wp_rest`) is the in-browser method and is NOT usable by a server-side connector. Recorded for completeness only.
AuthAlternatives.thirdPartyPlugins: OAuth 1.0a Server plugin / JWT plugins are mentioned by the handbook but are per-site and not declarable.

Configuration.TokenRefreshStrategyNote: NULL is the accurate answer, not a gap. Application Passwords and Woo consumer keys are long-lived credentials with no expiry and no refresh endpoint. There is nothing to refresh.
Configuration.APIBaseURLNote: 🚩 THERE IS NO VENDOR HOST. WordPress is self-hosted: the API base is the TENANT'S OWN site root plus the REST prefix (default `/wp-json`). The derived spec records this as the OpenAPI server `{site}/wp-json` with `site` a per-connection variable. No concrete host is recorded anywhere in this metadata, by design.
Configuration.APIBaseURLDerivationRule: NOT a credential field, but a binding instruction for code-builder: do NOT string-concatenate siteUrl + '/wp-json'. The REST prefix is filterable via rest_get_url_prefix(), and sites without pretty permalinks are reached as /?rest_route=/wp/v2/posts. Derive the API root from the site's advertised REST URL — the 'Link: <...>; rel="https://api.w.org/"' response header or the equivalent homepage <link> element — falling back to {siteUrl}/wp-json/ then {siteUrl}/?rest_route=/. Empirically confirmed on the probe target: HEAD http://localhost:8088/ returns 'Link: <http://localhost:8088/wp-json/>; rel="https://api.w.org/"'. This is recorded in the siteUrl schema description so a later implementer cannot hardcode the wrong assumption.
Configuration.APIVersioningNote: The version is a path segment inside the namespace: /wp-json/wp/v2/... and /wp-json/wc/v3/.... There is no header-based or accept-header-based versioning. NOTE: the namespace itself is the version unit here, so "the API version" is per-namespace, not global — wp/v2 and wc/v3 advance independently, and Woo additionally ships gated wc/v4 + wc/v4/graphql namespaces at these pins.
Configuration.universalPKNote: NOT EMITTED — deliberately unset. WordPress has no uniform PK: most collections key on an integer id, taxonomies / post types / post statuses key on slug, WooCommerce settings groups key on a string id, and WooCommerce /data endpoints key on a code. A blanket universalPK hint would mis-drive the runtime SoftPKClassifier for whole object families, so no hint is emitted and per-object PK determination is left to ioiof-extractor (only where explicit) or runtime D4.

PaginationDefaults.maxPageSizeEnforcement: server-side — a request above 100 is REJECTED, not silently clamped
PaginationDefaults.offsetParamNote: An `offset` param also exists on most collections and, where present, OVERRIDES page arithmetic.
PaginationDefaults.terminationRule: Stop when the page index exceeds X-WP-TotalPages, or when no `rel="next"` Link is present.
PaginationDefaults.appliesToWooNote: wc/v3 inherits the same base collection params, so the 100 cap applies to wc/v3 too. 🚩 The Woo DOCS do NOT state a cap — the SOURCE is the authority here.
PaginationDefaults.driftRisk: OFFSET-based, therefore DRIFT-PRONE under concurrent writes on deep pages: rows shift across page boundaries and a deep full scan can skip or duplicate records. Deep paging is also O(offset) in the database and that, not a documented cap on `page`, is the practical wall.
PaginationDefaults.driftMitigation: A STABLE SORT (orderby=id&order=asc). This reduces but does not eliminate the drift. The connector declares best-effort completeness for a deep full scan — it does NOT claim exactness. See DeclaredCapabilityLimits.offset-pagination-drift.

IncrementalSyncCapability.note: 🚩 UNEVEN, AND THE UNEVENNESS IS PER-CONTROLLER-BASE-CLASS, NOT PER-NAMESPACE. Whether a family supports a watermark is decided by which base class its controller extends, so it cannot be inferred from the namespace or from the docs. Two families that a naive reading treats as incremental are NOT: wp/v2/users and wc/v3/customers.

fullWatermark.families: wp/v2 posts, pages, media, blocks, templates, template-parts, navigation and ANY custom post type registered with show_in_rest; wc/v3 products, product variations, orders, order refunds (both /refunds and /orders/<id>/refunds), coupons.
fullWatermark.params: after / before (on date created) AND modified_after / modified_before, plus orderby=modified and a `modified` field on the record. Woo additionally accepts dates_are_gmt.
fullWatermark.evidence: wp-includes/rest-api/endpoints/class-wp-rest-posts-controller.php (modified_after/modified_before @since 5.7.0) ; woocommerce/includes/rest-api/Controllers/Version3/class-wc-rest-crud-controller.php:308,331,334,608,620 — defined ONCE on the shared CRUD base class

createdOnly.params: after / before on the creation date ONLY — no modified filter. Treat as insert-oriented; updates are invisible.

insertOnlyHighWater.params: orderby=registered_date only — NO date filter of any kind.
insertOnlyHighWater.note: This is the PRECISE capability, proven from source, and it is identical for both families. UPDATES REMAIN INVISIBLE. It must NOT be rounded up to "incremental supported", and NO IncrementalWatermarkField may be emitted. On wp/v2/users the ordering itself requires the `list_users` capability. See DeclaredCapabilityLimits.users-no-incremental and .woo-customers-no-incremental.

none.families: wc/v3/orders/<id>/notes ; and the config/reference resources — product attributes + attribute terms, product categories, product tags, product brands, product shipping classes, taxes, tax classes, shipping zones / zone locations / zone methods, shipping methods, payment gateways, settings groups, setting options, system status, system status tools, data (countries/currencies/continents), customer downloads.
none.note: No date filters and no modified fields. Full-scan only — acceptable, since these are small slow-changing reference sets.

IncrementalSyncCapability.deletes: NONE. See DeclaredCapabilityLimits.no-deleted-records-feed — there is no deleted-records feed anywhere, and deletion reconciliation is a declared KEY SWEEP, not detection.
IncrementalSyncCapability.inferenceRule: NEVER infer support from a 200 response — an unrecognised arg is SILENTLY IGNORED rather than rejected. Read the arg list from OPTIONS <route>.

Configuration.WebhooksNote: WooCommerce ONLY. wc/v3 registers a first-class webhooks resource — /wc/v3/webhooks, /wc/v3/webhooks/{id}, /wc/v3/webhooks/batch — present in the derived in-scope spec, with after/before (created date) collection params. WordPress CORE has NO webhook API at all: nothing in wp/v2 registers or delivers hooks. So webhook availability is conditional on WooCommerce being installed AND on the connection carrying a credential able to reach wc/v3.
Configuration.WebhooksSignatureGap: 🚩 GAP, deliberately left NULL rather than guessed. The webhook delivery/signing code (includes/class-wc-webhook.php) is NOT in the acquired pinned file set — the local Woo 11.0.1 extraction covers includes/rest-api, includes/admin and includes/wccom-site only. The signature algorithm and header name are therefore NOT PROVABLE from the pinned sources on this run, and no value is recorded. A later phase with the full plugin tree, or a live OPTIONS/delivery observation, must fill this in.
Configuration.BulkOperationsNote: 🚩 BATCHING IS WRITE-ONLY. READS ARE NOT BATCHABLE ANYWHERE. Stating this honestly because the naive read of "the API supports batch" is that a bulk read exists — it does not, in core or in Woo v3.

core.shape: a single request carrying a `requests[]` array of sub-requests
core.maxSubRequestsDiscovery: Read it from OPTIONS /batch/v1 — NEVER hardcode. It is server-tunable via `apply_filters( 'rest_get_max_batch_size', 25 )` at wp-includes/rest-api/class-wp-rest-server.php:1730.
core.validationMode: validation=require-all-validate — pre-validate every sub-request and atomically reject the whole batch on any failure.
core.enumerationTrap: /batch/v1 is registered as a route (class-wp-rest-server.php:115) but is ABSENT from the route index's `namespaces[]` array, so a namespaces[]-only enumeration misses it entirely. It is modelled here as a batch CAPABILITY on the Integration row, not as an IntegrationObject.

woocommerce.maxItemsTunable: apply_filters( 'woocommerce_rest_batch_items_limit', 100, <rest_base> ) at includes/rest-api/Controllers/Version3/class-wc-rest-controller.php:180 — per-resource AND per-site tunable.

BatchCapability.outOfScope: POST /wc/store/v1/batch — the Store API is out of scope for 1.0.0.

RateLimitPolicy.statement: 🚩 NOT VENDOR-DOCUMENTED for wp/v2 or wc/v3. WordPress core imposes NO rate limiting, and the WooCommerce v3 docs contain no rate-limit section. Verified: 0 occurrences of `RateLimit` anywhere in the derived in-scope spec, and a live GET /wp/v2/posts returned no RateLimit-* headers.
RateLimitPolicy.numbersDeliberatelyOmitted: NO NUMBER IS RECORDED, in this blob or in BatchMaxRequestCount / BatchRequestWaitTime. Emitting one would fabricate a vendor commitment that does not exist.
RateLimitPolicy.realWorld: Actual limits are HOST-IMPOSED and invisible to the vendor contract: managed WordPress hosts, CDNs/WAFs (Cloudflare, Sucuri), mod_security, PHP max_execution_time, and per-site security plugins. They vary per tenant and can change without notice.
RateLimitPolicy.connectorObligation: Honour HTTP 429 + Retry-After ADAPTIVELY; also back off on 503 and on connection resets. Use a conservative default concurrency, because the thing being loaded is the TENANT'S OWN SITE.
RateLimitPolicy.theOneException: The ONLY WordPress-ecosystem API with documented RateLimit-* headers is wc/store/v1 (the Store API), which is OUT OF SCOPE. And even there the defaults are OFF: src/StoreApi/Utilities/RateLimits.php has ENABLED = false, LIMIT = 25, SECONDS = 10, PROXY_SUPPORT = false — the headers appear only on sites that opted in.

ErrorResponseShape.note: The standard WP_Error JSON serialisation used by WP_REST_Server for every error across wp/v2, wc/v3 and /batch/v1. `code` is the stable machine-readable discriminator (e.g. rest_forbidden, rest_no_route, woocommerce_rest_authentication_error, woocommerce_rest_request_entity_too_large); `message` is localised and MUST NOT be parsed. Batch sub-request failures are reported per-item inside the batch response envelope, not as a top-level error.
ErrorResponseShape.evidenceStrength: ImpliedFromExample — the shape is consistent across every observed error and across the named error codes, but no single pinned document states it as a contract.

Configuration.CustomObjectMarkerNote: 🚩 WordPress has NO NAME-MARKER convention for custom objects — nothing analogous to HubSpot's `p_<accountID>_<name>`. A site-registered custom post type or custom taxonomy flows through the SAME core controllers as a built-in one, with only a different `rest_base`, and appears in the route index indistinguishable from core. Consequence: custom objects can be DISCOVERED (they are in the route index) but cannot be IDENTIFIED as custom by pattern-matching a name. The only reliable discriminator is set subtraction against the declared stock-install floor recorded in DeclaredAgainst. NULL here is correct, not missing.
Configuration.CustomFieldMarkerNote: Same story at the field level. Registered `meta` is a nested object whose keys are PER-SITE — only meta registered with show_in_rest appears — so the field universe is per-site too, independently of the per-site OBJECT universe. There is no marker pattern; per-site meta keys are discovered from OPTIONS, never inferred.
Configuration.WriteCapabilityNote: Deliberately NOT declared bidirectional. 'Bidirectional' would claim two-way SYNC semantics, and WordPress provides none of the machinery that requires: there is no change-log or deleted-records feed (hard deletes leave no tombstone), there are no ETags/If-Match concurrency tokens on the in-scope routes, wp/v2/users and wc/v3/customers expose no modified timestamp at all so their remote state cannot even be diffed, and offset pagination cannot guarantee a complete scan. Reads and writes are both fully supported, but the vendor gives no conflict-resolution or change-capture primitive to build a safe two-way loop on. read-write is the honest ceiling.
Configuration.WriteCapabilityBindingNote: BINDING under the floor rule capability-dishonest. The connector may declare and implement create/update/delete. It may NOT declare bidirectional sync, and it must NOT claim delete DETECTION (only a declared key-sweep).
Configuration.WriteShape: Core: POST /wp/v2/<collection> (create); POST or PUT/PATCH /wp/v2/<collection>/<id> (update); DELETE /wp/v2/<collection>/<id> (soft-delete to trash for post types, ?force=true for hard delete). Woo wc/v3: the same, plus per-resource batch. Ordinary JSON request bodies; readOnly properties are marked in each get_item_schema().
Configuration.ConcurrencyControlNote: PROVEN ABSENT for the in-scope surface: 0 occurrences of If-Match, If-Unmodified-Since or ETag anywhere in the derived in-scope spec, and no request parameter in wp/v2 or wc/v3 accepts a client-supplied version token. 🚩 One evidenced caveat that is NOT a concurrency primitive: Woo 11.0.1 contains an ETag-GENERATION hook — `get_data_for_etag()` overridden in includes/rest-api/Controllers/Version2/class-wc-rest-products-v2-controller.php:104 (it strips the randomly-sampled `related_ids` before hashing) — and that method is the ONLY ETag reference in the entire includes/rest-api tree; the base class that CALLS it lies outside the acquired file set. That is response-CACHING machinery, not an optimistic-concurrency token a client can send back, so it is unusable as a conflict primitive at these pins and ConcurrencyControl stays `none`.
Configuration.DeleteSemanticsDetail: SOFT for post types (DELETE moves to `status=trash`, and trashed records remain listable via status=trash). HARD for everything else, and hard for post types when `?force=true` is passed — a hard delete leaves NO tombstone. Orphan deletion is therefore NOT safe to infer from absence; it requires the declared key sweep. See DeclaredCapabilityLimits.no-deleted-records-feed.
Configuration.DefaultSyncDirectionNote: READ-ONLY BY DEFAULT for every object, per the read-first / bidirectional-opt-in rule. Writes are fully supported by the vendor and may be implemented, but push/create/update/delete against a client's real site must be validated against a sandbox FIRST. Preconditions before bidirectional could ever be enabled for this vendor: (1) a change-capture primitive for the families that have none (wp/v2/users, wc/v3/customers) — there is none today; (2) a deletion signal — there is none, only a key sweep; (3) a concurrency token to make conflict resolution safe — there is none. All three are absent, so bidirectional is not merely off-by-default here, it is not currently justifiable.
Configuration.DefaultConflictResolutionReason: ConcurrencyControl is `none`, so `MostRecent` MUST NOT be recommended — there is no ETag or version token, and two of the in-scope families (wp/v2/users, wc/v3/customers) expose no modified timestamp at all, so their remote state cannot even be diffed to decide which side is newer. With no vendor primitive to arbitrate, `Manual` is the only honest default.
Configuration.DiscoveryIsAuthoritativeRationale: The two levels differ and ONE BOOLEAN CANNOT EXPRESS BOTH, so DiscoveryIsAuthoritative stays FALSE — the safe default — and the nuance lives here. Field-level deactivation is flatly unsafe (a thin context=view schema would delete real fields). Object-level deactivation is ALSO unsafe once the gating above is admitted: a namespace can vanish from one site's index because of a feature flag or a lazy-load filter while remaining a real part of the vendor's surface. Record the object-level authority as an OBSERVATION, never as a deactivation licence.

DiscoveryAuthoritativeness.objectLevelNote: GET {base}/wp-json enumerates every route the site has REGISTERED for that request, and route REGISTRATION is not capability-gated — an under-privileged credential still sees the full route list (only the responses 401). That makes the route index an authoritative enumeration of what THAT CONNECTION can ever address. It is NOT an enumeration of what the SOFTWARE can expose.
DiscoveryAuthoritativeness.objectLevelRejectionReason: DEVIATION D1. The plan's literal value overstates the guarantee and is disproven three ways at the pinned versions (see objectLevelCaveats). A later reader must not treat 'complete-route-index' as licence to deactivate objects that a feature flag or a lazy-load filter merely hid on one site at one moment.

objectLevelCaveats.detail: WooCommerce LAZY-LOADS namespaces per request via wc_rest_should_load_namespace() (includes/wc-rest-functions.php, since Woo 9.2) over a known_namespaces list of wc/v1, wc/v2, wc/v3, wc/v4, wc-telemetry, wc-admin, wc-analytics, wc/store, wc/private — and the decision is exposed through the public `wc_rest_should_load_namespace` filter, so ANY site can override which namespaces appear.

Whole namespaces sit behind FEATURE FLAGS and are therefore absent from a stock route index while being fully present in the shipped software: wc/v4 requires Features::is_enabled('rest-api-v4'), which defaults FALSE (includes/rest-api/Server.php:83; includes/react-admin/feature-config.php:42 'rest-api-v4' => false), and wc/v4/graphql requires the `dual_code_graphql_api` feature plus PHP 8.1+. Both ship in Woo 11.0.1 and both were verified absent from a stock index (0 live wc/v4 routes).

/batch/v1 is a registered ROUTE (wp-includes/rest-api/class-wp-rest-server.php:115) that never appears in the route index's `namespaces[]` array at all — the reference instance reports its namespace as EMPTY. A namespaces[]-only enumeration silently misses it.

DiscoveryAuthoritativeness.fieldLevelNote: OPTIONS <route> returns a real JSON Schema, but field visibility IS capability-gated (context=edit plus the corresponding capability). An under-privileged credential legitimately receives a THINNER schema than the docs describe, so field ABSENCE at runtime proves NOTHING about the vendor.
DiscoveryAuthoritativeness.deactivationPermittedWhy: The two levels differ and ONE BOOLEAN CANNOT EXPRESS BOTH, so DiscoveryIsAuthoritative stays FALSE — the safe default — and the nuance lives here. Field-level deactivation is flatly unsafe (a thin context=view schema would delete real fields). Object-level deactivation is ALSO unsafe once the gating above is admitted: a namespace can vanish from one site's index because of a feature flag or a lazy-load filter while remaining a real part of the vendor's surface. Record the object-level authority as an OBSERVATION, never as a deactivation licence.

DeclaredAgainst.note: The declared catalog is a STOCK-INSTALL SNAPSHOT at these exact versions, derived deterministically from register_routes() + get_item_schema() in the pinned PHP source. 🚩 WITHOUT THESE PINS NOBODY CAN TELL LATER whether a "missing" object means the connector is wrong or the site is simply older (or newer).
DeclaredAgainst.knownPinSkew: Woo 11.0.1 declares "tested up to" WP 7.0.4, i.e. it is NOT yet declared-tested against WP 7.1. This is a real, documented skew in the pin pair and is recorded rather than smoothed over.

Configuration.ObjectUniverseScopeNote: WordPress's object universe is per-SITE, not per-vendor: plugins add whole namespaces, and sites register custom post types and custom taxonomies that flow through the SAME core controllers with a different rest_base. So the DECLARED catalog is the stock-install FLOOR at the pinned versions, and the PER-CONNECTION ROUTE INDEX is the truth. 🚩 DECLARED IS NEVER A CEILING. The per-site remainder is reachable only by the connector's runtime route-index discovery, which on this credential-free [B]-posture run is UNVERIFIED rather than covered.

DeclaredCapabilityLimits.reason: wp/v2/users exposes NO date filter and NO modified timestamp. get_collection_params() yields exactly: context, page, per_page, search, search_columns, exclude, include, offset, order, orderby, slug, roles, capabilities, who, has_published_posts — and the string 'modified' does not occur anywhere in class-wp-rest-users-controller.php (0 occurrences, independently reproduced). The record schema DOES carry `registered_date`, and `orderby` DOES accept `registered_date` (mapped to WP_User_Query orderby `registered` at class-wp-rest-users-controller.php:310).
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.capabilityPrecise: FULL-SCAN, or at most an INSERT-ONLY HIGH-WATER scan ordered by registered_date. This narrow capability is PROVEN, not assumed — but UPDATES to existing users are INVISIBLE to any delta strategy, because no modified timestamp exists to compare against.
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.consequence: No IncrementalWatermarkField may be emitted on users. No delta test cell may simulate one. The insert-only high-water capability may be declared EXACTLY as stated and must never be rounded up to "incremental supported".
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.additionalGate: The insert-only high-water path is ITSELF capability-gated: class-wp-rest-users-controller.php:228 rejects orderby=registered_date (and orderby=email) unless the caller has `list_users`. An under-privileged credential therefore loses even this narrow capability and degrades to unordered full-scan.

DeclaredCapabilityLimits.reason: DEVIATION D2 — NOT in the script's literal limit list. wc/v3/customers does NOT extend WC_REST_CRUD_Controller. The chain is WC_REST_Customers_Controller -> WC_REST_Customers_V2_Controller -> WC_REST_Customers_V1_Controller -> WC_REST_Controller -> WP_REST_Controller (independently reproduced from the class declarations), so it inherits NONE of the date params defined on WC_REST_CRUD_Controller: no `after`, no `before`, no `modified_after`, no `dates_are_gmt` (0 occurrences of any of them across all three customers controller files; contrast class-wc-rest-crud-controller.php:308,331,334,608,620 where they are all defined).
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.capabilityPrecise: FULL-SCAN, or an INSERT-ONLY HIGH-WATER scan via orderby=registered_date — EXACTLY the same narrow capability as wp/v2/users, not a weaker one and not a full watermark. Proven: the orderby enum [id, include, name, registered_date] at class-wc-rest-customers-v1-controller.php:1027, mapped to WP_User_Query orderby `registered` at :358.
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.consequence: UPDATES INVISIBLE. No watermark field on customers, and no simulated customers delta cell. This entry exists because the context notes' phrasing ("WooCommerce orders/products support modified_after") would lead straight to emitting a watermark on customers that does not exist.

DeclaredCapabilityLimits.reason: There is NO deleted-records feed anywhere in wp/v2 or wc/v3. `status=trash` covers SOFT deletes for post types ONLY; a hard delete (DELETE ?force=true) vanishes leaving NO tombstone of any kind.
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.consequence: Deletion reconciliation requires a periodic KEY SWEEP (compare the full remote ID set against the local set). The connector must DECLARE the key sweep rather than pretend to DETECT deletions. It must not claim delete detection.

DeclaredCapabilityLimits.reason: Many fields are exposed only for context=edit PLUS the corresponding capability (e.g. a user's email and registered_date). OPTIONS <route> returns a real JSON Schema, but the schema a caller receives is filtered by that caller's capabilities.
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.consequence: An under-privileged credential SILENTLY returns a THINNER schema than the docs describe. Field ABSENCE at runtime therefore proves NOTHING about the vendor, and NO discovery result may deactivate a declared field. The derived catalog is the MAXIMUM a fully-privileged credential sees, not a per-connection guarantee.

DeclaredCapabilityLimits.reason: `page`/`per_page` is OFFSET-based page numbering, not keyset/cursor. Concurrent writes shift rows across page boundaries during a deep scan, so records can be skipped or duplicated.
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.consequence: Completeness of a deep full-scan is BEST-EFFORT. The mitigation is a stable sort (orderby=id&order=asc), which reduces but does not eliminate drift. Exactness must never be claimed.

DeclaredCapabilityLimits.reason: One connection may need TWO credential shapes: an Application Password for wp/v2, and optionally a WooCommerce consumer key/secret for wc/v3. A Woo-only key pair CANNOT read wp/v2 at all — WC_REST_Authentication::is_request_to_rest_api() matches only URIs whose path after the REST prefix begins `wc/` or `wc-`.
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.consequence: A partially-provisioned credential yields a PARTIAL object set. That must surface as an EXPLICIT capability warning, never as an empty-but-green sync. Additionally, Application Passwords are unavailable over plain HTTP outside a local environment (wp-includes/user.php:5156 `return is_ssl() || 'local' === wp_get_environment_type();`), which is why the credential schema expresses the two pairs as `anyOf` rather than both hard-required.

DeclaredCapabilityLimits.fact: The vendor DOES support writing site settings — POST /wp/v2/settings with a flat body, no {id} segment. But wp/v2/settings is a SINGLETON: one row, addressed with no identifier at all, so the object has no primary key (PK deliberately unset at extraction — identity genuinely absent).
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.consequence: MJ save paths identify a row by primary key, so a writable object with no PK cannot be saved (the lint-writable-pk gate rejects it, and on PostgreSQL the write could not execute). This connector therefore declares the write surface UNAVAILABLE for Setting rather than fabricating an identity the vendor does not expose. Reads are unaffected.
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.classification: FRAMEWORK EXPRESSIVENESS GAP, not a vendor limitation — MJ cannot currently express a writable singleton. If that is added, restore SupportsWrite/SupportsUpdate plus UpdateAPIPath=/wp/v2/settings, UpdateMethod=POST, UpdateBodyShape=flat, UpdateIDLocation=n/a.

Configuration.DeclaredCapabilityLimitsNote: Six machine-readable entries, each an honest limitation that a lazy build would paper over with a fake test cell. `woo-customers-no-incremental` is DEVIATION D2 — it is not in the plan's literal list and was added on SourceAudit/BrandResearch evidence. Each entry carries scope + reason + consequence, and the two insert-only families carry `capabilityPrecise` so the narrow proven capability is not rounded up.
Configuration.AsyncOperationModelNote: FULLY SYNCHRONOUS. No route in wp/v2, wc/v3 or /batch/v1 returns a job id, a 202-plus-poll handle, or an export-file handle — every request returns the final representation. WordPress does have background infrastructure (WP-Cron; Woo bundles Action Scheduler) but neither is exposed as a REST job API in the in-scope surface, so there is nothing to poll. Consequence: large extractions are bounded by per_page <= 100 and by request-time limits on the TENANT'S OWN host, not by a job queue — throughput is a function of the customer's hosting, which the connector cannot know in advance.

FilterSearchModel.note: There is NO generic filter DSL (no OData-style $filter, no arbitrary field predicates) — only the enumerated per-route args. An unrecognised arg is silently ignored rather than rejected, so a connector must never infer support from a 200 response; it must read the arg list from OPTIONS.
FilterSearchModel.core: `search` (free text) on every collection, plus `search_columns` to restrict which columns are searched, plus per-collection filters: status, author, author_exclude, categories, categories_exclude, tags, tags_exclude, slug, sticky, ignore_sticky, format, tax_relation, parent, parent_exclude, include, exclude, offset, order, orderby. FilterSearchModel.woo: `search`, plus per-resource: status, type, sku, category, tag, attribute, attribute_term, on_sale, min_price, max_price, stock_status, featured, customer, product, created_via, reviewer, reviewer_email, role, email, code.
